name: gitdiagram
description: Free, simple, fast interactive diagrams for any GitHub repository
one_liner: Turns any GitHub codebase into a clickable diagram of how it's put together, in seconds, so a new hire or reviewer can understand the system without reading every file.
buyer: An engineering manager onboarding new hires who wastes hours walking people through 'how the codebase fits together' every time someone joins.
business_use_cases: A company adds it to onboarding docs so new engineers get an instant visual map of the codebase before their first 1-on-1 walkthrough.
A due-diligence firm evaluating a startup's codebase (for acquisition or investment) uses it to quickly understand architecture without a lengthy code review.
An open-source maintainer embeds a generated diagram in the README to help contributors orient themselves without asking basic questions in issues.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a paid private-repo tier with saved, shareable diagrams for team documentation
Sell 'codebase onboarding kits' (diagram plus written architecture summary) as a one-off service for teams

steal_this: This weekend, offer a fixed-price 'instant architecture report' service for messy legacy codebases: diagram plus a plain-English writeup a new hire could actually use.
